question: What type of data is represented by numbers like birth weight in clinical research?
explanation: Numbers and measurements collected in a study are classified as quantitative data. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why do midwifery researchers use statistical analysis on raw data?

options.A: To prove personal opinions are correct
options.B: To hide errors made during data collection
options.C: To make the research paper look longer
options.D: To turn messy numbers into clear patterns

explanation: Statistics help organize and analyze raw figures so researchers can see meaningful trends and differences. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h1)

question: What does a p-value measure in a clinical research study?

options.A: The probability that results happened by chance
options.B: The exact cost of running the clinical trial
options.C: The total number of pregnant women in the study
options.D: The percentage of staff who conducted interviews

explanation: The p-value tells researchers how likely it is that their findings occurred purely due to random variation. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h2)

question: What does a traditional p-value threshold of less than 0.05 mean for a study?

options.A: The study took less than five weeks to complete
options.B: At least 5% of the babies born will have health issues
options.C: Five patients dropped out before the trial ended
options.D: There is less than a 5% chance the results are a fluke

explanation: A p-value below 0.05 indicates strong evidence against pure luck, meaning less than a 5% probability of random occurrence. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h2)

question: What does statistical significance indicate about research findings?

options.A: The data collection process had zero errors
options.B: The treatment is affordable for rural clinics
options.C: Every patient in the study was cured completely
options.D: A reliable difference unlikely due to chance

explanation: Statistical significance confirms that the numerical difference found between groups is likely real and not a random fluke. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h3)

question: A study of 5,000 women finds a new herb reduces postpartum bleeding duration by one minute (p = 0.001). What best describes this finding?

options.A: It is statistically significant but has low clinical relevance
options.B: It is clinically vital and should change national policy
options.C: It is both statistically and clinically useless
options.D: It proves the study data was collected incorrectly

explanation: A very small time difference can meet statistical thresholds due to a large sample size, yet fail to matter practically for patient care. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why is assuming correlation equals causation a dangerous mistake in healthcare research?

options.A: Two factors appearing together do not prove one caused the other
options.B: It always results in patients receiving expired medications
options.C: It stops hospitals from buying new delivery beds
options.D: It means the statistical software was definitely hacked

explanation: Variables can move together due to a third hidden factor rather than a direct cause-and-effect relationship. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h4)

question: What does a high p-value above 0.05 actually mean for a tested intervention?

options.A: The treatment is proven to be dangerous for mothers
options.B: The research participants lied on their questionnaires
options.C: The study lacked enough evidence to prove an effect
options.D: The medical equipment used was completely broken

explanation: A non-significant p-value means we cannot rule out chance, not that we have definitive proof the treatment does nothing. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h4)

question: When applying international research findings to a local Nigerian clinic, what must a midwife consider?

options.A: Whether the original researchers speak the local language
options.B: Whether local resources and patient contexts match the study
options.C: If the research paper has colorful pictures and charts
options.D: How many awards the primary author won for the study

explanation: Evidence must fit the local clinical setting, staff capacity, and available supplies before it can be safely adopted. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h5)

question: What does the term generalizability mean when reading a research paper?

options.A: Whether the introduction section is written clearly
options.B: How many generals or high-ranking officers funded the study
options.C: How fast the statistical software generated the p-value
options.D: Whether the findings apply to other populations and settings

explanation: Generalizability refers to how well study results can be extended beyond the specific group of people tested. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T4#BMP225_U4_T4_h5)
